edges.description: Untreated caries progressing to periapical infection of a mandibular molar is the route to the submandibular space, because those roots sit below the mylohyoid line. Dental decay is the known intermediate between poor hygiene and this node.

Diabetes targets the cellulitis rather than the dental origin because it is a host factor permitting spread once infection exists rather than a cause of the odontogenic source. The route is not established here: the cited evidence is a comorbidity list from a single case report and names no mechanism.
An iatrogenic route to the same node: extraction opens the mandibular molar socket directly into the fascial planes, which is why this presentation follows a dental procedure rather than neglect.
Preceding viral infection is proposed to impair mucosal defence and permit bacterial invasion, but the available evidence here is a single co-occurrence report rather than an association study.
Acts through access to dental care rather than through any biological route: untreated caries is what supplies the odontogenic source, and cost is what leaves it untreated.

evidence.snippet: Ninety-two percent (n=57/62) of the streptococci cultured were sensitive to penicillin. The addition of aminoglycosides to the study sample would not have made a statistically significant difference (p=0.1556).

nodes.description: The streptococci and oral anaerobes that drive Ludwig's angina build their peptidoglycan cell wall by penicillin-binding protein (PBP) transpeptidase cross-linking. This essential, bacteria-specific reaction is the target of the penicillin/beta-lactam component of empiric broad-spectrum therapy; culture series show the predominant streptococci remain penicillin-sensitive, so acylation of the PBP active site halts cross-linking and is bactericidal.

evidence.reference_title: From the regulation of peptidoglycan synthesis to bacterial growth and morphology.
evidence.snippet: although glycan chain polymerization occurs in the absence of transpeptidation (for example, in the presence of penicillin), efficient transpeptidation requires ongoing GTase reactions
